title: Root-Uptake Attribution Exact-Forcing Binding Remediation

source_authority_current_recheck.disposition: continue exact source-bound remediation from frozen authority

runtime_trace.physical_forcing_binding: mod_fmr_serialized_reference_backend:fmr_serialized_prepare_interval copies forcing%root_extraction_sink into worker-local self%qrot before the physical solve
runtime_trace.candidate_creation: mod_fmr_serialized_multiswap_runtime:execute_column passes forcing_registry(forcing_index) directly into backend%run_trial and receives the candidate in the same stack frame
runtime_trace.commit_boundary: the same execute_column stack frame commits that candidate and optionally obtains fmr_accepted_commit_receipt_t
runtime_trace.forcing_identity_available: forcing_index remains bound to column%forcing_handle throughout that transaction

remediation_design.public_api_rule: no public API may accept an already-created candidate together with an independently supplied qrot forcing
remediation_design.execution_rule: the wrapper invokes the existing serialized physical runtime and derives root-uptake attribution only from the same forcing_registry supplied to that invocation and only for ready accepted-commit receipts returned by it
remediation_design.publication_rule: attribution is postcommit reconciliation metadata only and is never added to generic mass_out
remediation_design.state_rule: receipt state is ephemeral output; no committed column state or solver scratch is added
remediation_design.scope: restricted serialized real physics; parallel root-extraction execution remains excluded

owner_gates: positive committed root-uptake amount equals exact qrot integral
F-VQ48 candidate/forcing re-pairing seam no longer exists in the production API
two different forcing cases each publish their own exact amount without cross-contamination
rejected/uncommitted requested column emits no ready attribution
invalid sparse attribution requests fail before physical mutation through the existing receipt-request gate
attribution amount is a subset of existing mass_out and does not alter mass diagnostics
